chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: When a man enters into the state of Ihram after the prescribed prayer, should he recite the Talbiyah when he rises with his camel, or while seated after the prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: He may do whichever of those he desires.

Al-Kulayni said: And this, in my view, is from the matters of ease (permissibility), except that the merit in it is that he should manifest the Talbiyah where the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) manifested it, at the edge of Al-Bayda', and it is not permissible for anyone to exceed a mile of Al-Bayda' unless he has already manifested the Talbiyah; and the first of Al-Bayda' is the first mile that meets you on the left of the road.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَة: The ritual declaration 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk' recited during Hajj
key_terms.الْبَيْدَاء: A specific location near Mecca, traditionally associated with the Prophet's Ihram

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim recite the Talbiyah for Hajj: before mounting the camel or after?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the flexibility in the timing of the Talbiyah, allowing it to be recited either while seated after the preparatory prayer or upon mounting the mount. Al-Kulayni contextualizes this permissibility by linking it to the Prophet’s practice at Al-Bayda', defining the optimal moment for declaration while setting a boundary that one should not travel beyond a mile without reciting it. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ease (tawassu') with adherence to the Sunnah of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his progeny).
